answer: FAIL_F6. The PR's own embedded multispectrum file lists only 3 alternatives ('keep retired dir', 'move to registry/capability-templates', 'add new ADR') and rejects them in one-line trade-offs — this is below F6 floor for CC-3 (need 3+ named with Linus-style AND hyperscaler-style per load-bearing decision). Four load-bearing decisions ship with NO options table: (D1) directory location — `registry/capability-templates/` was chosen as a new fragmenting root rather than landing under the existing `registries/cross-cutting/` canonical control-plane root (which would match the docs/AGENTS.md taxonomy and avoid yet another top-level registry sibling); (D2) versioning policy — both `capability-record-template.yaml` and `capability-record-template-v2.yaml` are kept side-by-side with no deprecation plan, when single-source-of-truth (delete v1 when v2 lands) is the canonical Oyatie discipline per the no-silent-regression and ADR-0064 doctrine; (D3) PR granularity — one 44-file blob touches CLI defaults + 6 ADRs + 9 docs + 3 templates + registry rows + 7 .omc project-memory tmp files in a single merge; F1-style discipline would split into ≥5 concern-scoped PRs (registry move, CLI defaults, ADR amendments, doc renames, template path edits) so each can be reviewed and reverted independently; (D4) ADR posture — five existing ADRs (0003, 0007, 0019, 0050, 0052) are amended in-place to swap `product-control/` → `registry/capability-templates/` without writing a new ADR that records the topology rename rationale; the in-PR evidence explicitly rejects an ADR ('would duplicate topology rationale already represented by the task') but a path move that mutates five ratified ADRs IS the canonical trigger for a superseding/amending ADR per ADR-0019 update protocol. The author's selected_rationale leans on ADR-0116 'already covers Foundry-pipeline VCS/tooling cutover' but ADR-0116 is not cited in the diff hunks for the amended ADRs, so the linkage is unverified.
alternatives_considered: ==DECISION 1: DIRECTORY LOCATION (PR chose; F6 supplies competitors)==
A: registry/capability-templates/ at repo root (CHOSEN). Adds a new top-level registry sibling next to registry/catalog/, registry/audit-chain/, registry/foundation-bypasses/, etc.

B [canonical-fit]: registries/cross-cutting/capability-templates/ — lands under the existing cross-cutting registries root mentioned in CLAUDE.md root-hub-pointers and matches the cross-cutting axis taxonomy. Cost: deeper path, more typing in CLI defaults; Benefit: zero new top-level fragmentation, aligns with established control-plane root.

C [Linus-style]: registry/foundry/capabilities/ — scope to the consuming axis (Foundry) rather than inventing a new generic 'capability-templates' bucket. Cost: less generic; Benefit: ownership is unambiguous, no cross-axis confusion if Cloud/Data axes later also want capability records.

D [hyperscaler-style]: control-plane/capabilities/<id>/{template.yaml,eval-set.yaml,eval-run.yaml} — colocate the three related artifacts under one capability-id directory (Stripe/AWS-style). Cost: directory-per-capability bloat for small catalogs; Benefit: discoverability and atomic per-capability ownership.
==DECISION 2: TEMPLATE VERSIONING POLICY (PR kept both v1+v2; F6 supplies)==
A: Keep capability-record-template.yaml AND capability-record-template-v2.yaml side-by-side (CHOSEN by omission — both files are edited in the PR but neither is deleted).

B [no-silent-regression]: Delete v1 the moment v2 lands; single source of truth; force consumers off legacy. Aligns with the project's own [No silent regression] feedback note and avoids template-drift bugs.
C: Mark v1 with explicit `sunset_after:` frontmatter and a sunset lane (lean-a-template-sunset) that fails CI after the cutover date. Compromise between (A) and (B).
==DECISION 3: PR GRANULARITY (PR chose monolith; F6 supplies)==
A: One 44-file PR covering registry move + CLI defaults + 5 ADR amendments + 9 doc renames + 3 template edits + 7 .omc tmp files (CHOSEN).

B [F1/Linus-style]: 5 concern-scoped PRs — (b1) git-mv registry files + add registry rows; (b2) CLI default-path swap with test update; (b3) ADR amendments as a single doc-only PR with explicit citation block; (b4) docs/templates path rename; (b5) .omc/project-memory tmp file purge (should arguably never be committed at all — see D5 below). Each is independently revertable and reviewable.

C [hyperscaler-style]: 2 PRs — (c1) introduce new path, dual-write registry rows for both old and new locations behind a feature flag, run for one cycle; (c2) remove old path. Safer cutover for a path that CI gates reference.
==DECISION 4: ADR POSTURE (PR chose 'amend 5 ADRs in place'; F6 supplies)==
A: Amend ADR-0003 / 0007 / 0019 / 0050 / 0052 in-place to swap path strings; no new ADR (CHOSEN, rationale: 'covered by ADR-0116').

B [ADR-0019 compliant]: Write ADR-0117 'Capability template registry topology cutover from product-control/ to registry/capability-templates/' as a small superseding ADR that the 5 amended ADRs link forward to. Cost: one extra file; Benefit: the move is traceable in the decisions index, not buried in PR body text.

C [minimum-trace]: Leave the 5 ADRs untouched and add a single ADDENDUM file (docs/decisions/addenda/path-cutover-2026-05-16.md) that records the global string substitution. Avoids rewriting ratified ADRs while preserving forensic intent.
==DECISION 5 (BONUS — F6 identified): .OMC PROJECT-MEMORY TMP FILES==
A: Commit 7 .omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.* files into the PR (CHOSEN — see files [0..6] in pr-15-meta.json).

B: .omc/.project-memory.json.tmp.* should be in .gitignore — these are tool tmp files; committing them pollutes git history and the diff. Alternative: add to .gitignore and `git rm --cached` in a follow-up cleanup PR.

recommendation: BLOCK. Require: (1) author surfaces D1-D5 alternatives in evidence file with explicit Linus + hyperscaler trade-off per decision; (2) write ADR-0117 (or addendum) recording the topology cutover per ADR-0019 protocol; (3) split into ≥3 PRs (registry/CLI move; ADR amendments; doc renames); (4) decide v1-vs-v2 template policy explicitly; (5) gitignore .omc/*.tmp.*. If splitting is refused, at minimum add the missing alternatives table and the superseding ADR within this PR before merge.
